sentences.text: This appeal has been filed under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) by the claim petitioner in O.P.(MV) No.796/2018 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Kozhikode (the Tribunal), aggrieved by the amount of compensation granted by Award dated 29/10/2019.
The respondents herein are the respondents in the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and the documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioner, on 25/12/2017 at about 12:30 a.m., while he was travelling in car bearing registration no. KL-11-BE-9955 from Feroke to 2025:KER:40814 Pantheerankavu and when reached the place by name Adivaram, the car hit an electric post, as a result of which the claim petitioner sustained grievous injuries.
3. The first respondent owner cum driver of the car remained ex parte.
4. The second respondent/insurer filed written statement admitting the policy, but disputing the liability.
There was no negligence on the part of the first respondent.
Averments in the petition regarding age, occupation and injuries sustained to the claim petitioner were disputed.
The amount of compensation claimed was contended to be excessive.
5. Before the Tribunal, no oral evidence was adduced by either side.
Exts.A1 to A11 and Ext.C1 were marked on the side of the claim petitioner.
No documentary evidence was adduced by the second respondent.

6. The Tribunal on consideration of the 2025:KER:40814 documentary evidence and after hearing both sides, found negligence on the part of the first respondent-driver of the offending vehicle resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 1,86,100/- together with interest at 8%
per annum from the date of the petition till realisation along with proportionate costs.
Aggrieved by the Award, the claim petitioner has come up in appeal.
7. The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.
8. Heard both sides 9.
The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following heads are challenged by the claim petitioner- Notional Income
The learned counsel for the claim petitioner submits that an amount of 25,000/- was stated to be the monthly income of 2025:KER:40814 the claim petitioner.

However,
the Tribunal fixed an amount of 10,000/- only as notional income, which is quite low and hence the same requires to be enhanced.

No oral or documentary evidence was produced to substantiate the same.

Hence in the light of the dictum in Ramachandrappa v. Manager, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd,
(2011) 13 SCC 236, I find that fixing the notional income at 11,000/- would be just and reasonable.

sentences.text: .A2 wound certificate refers to the injuries sustained by the claim petitioner.
They are - "Lacerated wound 1 x 0.5 x 0.5 cm upper lateral incisor lacerated wound 0.5 x 0.5 x 0.5 cm avulsion of tooth fracture frontal bone."
The records reveal that he was hospitalised for a period of three days.

As per Ext.C1 report, the Medical Board assessed his permanent disability as 7% based on the injuries sustained, that is,
"avulsed and lost upper left central and lateral incisors".

Ext.C1 reads - 2025:KER:40814 "We after careful examination of Sri/Smt. Vishnu Prasad, S/o.Vinod,
Mammalappil house, Kolasseriparamba, Thiruvannur-673029, whose signature is given above,
certify that He/She is having avulsed and lost upper left central and lateral incisors and is physically handicapped.
His/Her percentage of permanent disability due to the injury is seven (7%) and occupational disability due to the injury is- Dental - Oral and maxillofacial surgery."
The Medical Board in Ext.C1 has not certified that any functional or occupational disability has been caused to the claim petitioner.

In the decision cited, the opinion of the Medical board reads - "(a) Permanent privation of the sight of either eye or the hearing or either ear or any member of joint (mention if any): Now the patient has no speech and his intellectual functions are completely impaired.
He cannot stand and walk.
He is catheterized till now.
2025:KER:40814 (b) Destruction or permanent impairing of the power of any member of joint mention (if any).
He is dependent on others on Activities of Daily Living (ADL) = 100%.
He falls from bad (sic) several times.
He got many times during infection.
Total permanent, physical impairment is 100%.

sentences.text:
(d) The other material observation having adverse bearing on the life expectancy or nor-mal functioning of the body/limb injured/affected: Total Permanent Impairment is 100% one hundred percent."
(Emphasis supplied)
The Tribunal in the said case did not accept the report of the Medical Board on the ground that it was completely unreliable.

It was in the said circumstance, the Apex Court held that if the Tribunal had any reason(s) to doubt the medical certificate, the option that was available before it was to have the disability re- assessed and that the Tribunal ought not to have gone into the 2025:KER:40814 details of the determination of disability.

The dictum in Prakash Chand Sharma (Supra) cannot be applied to the facts of the present case because the Tribunal has not questioned the competency of the experts or rejected Ext.C1 saying that it was unreliable.
It only held that in the light of the injuries sustained and relying on the dictum in Thomas (Supra), compensation under this head cannot be granted.

In Thomas (Supra),
the question that was considered by a Division Bench of this Court was whether loss of front right upper incisor tooth of the claimant therein would amount to a permanent disability as defined under Section 142 of the Act.
This was answered in the negative.
In the case on hand also, the claim petitioner is seen to have lost his upper left central and lateral incisors.
Therefore the argument advanced that the dictum is not applicable to the facts of the present case does not seem to be right.

The learned counsel for the claim petitioner also submitted that due to the frontal bone fracture, occupational disability was caused to the claim petitioner and being a mechanic, he was unable to communicate properly/effectively with his customers.

This is something which comes under loss of amenities for which an amount of 1,00,000/- has been granted by the Tribunal,
though an amount of 50,000/- only was claimed.
In these circumstances, I find no reasons to interfere with the findings of the Tribunal on the said aspect.

In the result, the appeal is partly allowed by enhancing the compensation by a further amount of 1,000/- (total compensation 1,87,100/- that is, 1,86,100/- granted by the Tribunal + 1,000/- granted in appeal) with interest at the rate of 8% per annum from the date of petition till date of realization and proportionate costs.
The second respondent/insurance company is directed to deposit the aforesaid amount before the Tribunal within a period of 60 days from the date of receipt of a copy of the judgment.
On deposit of the amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the amount to the claim petitioner at the earliest in accordance with law after making deductions, if any.
Interlocutory applications, if any pending, shall stand closed.
